description: Astro Minds aims to develop an innovative health monitoring solution for astronauts. The system will monitor important health parameters, analyze health data, identify potential risks, and provide timely alerts and insights. Our goal is to support astronaut health and safety during space missions using modern technology, data analysis, and AI-based approaches.
summary:
ASTRA-3D is a software-based astronaut health monitoring system designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions. Space conditions can cause health risks such as cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, sleep disturbances, radiation exposure, and vision problems.

Our system provides a centralized dashboard to monitor astronaut health indicators, view crew information, identify unusual readings, and display health alerts. It is designed to support multiple astronauts and help mission control and medical teams review health conditions. The prototype uses sample or simulated readings for demonstration. In the future, it can be extended with validated NASA research datasets and compatible medical devices.

The main goal is to support early identification of potential health risks and improve astronaut health monitoring during space missions.
details:
ASTRA-3D is a software-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

Space missions can expose astronauts to health risks such as cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, sleep disturbances, radiation exposure, and vision-related problems.

Our solution provides a centralized dashboard to view astronaut health indicators, monitor multiple crew members, identify unusual readings, and display health alerts. It also includes health trend visualization and a 3D digital-twin concept to help mission control understand crew health information.

The prototype demonstrates its monitoring and alert workflow using sample and simulated readings. These readings are clearly distinguished from real medical-device measurements. The system is designed to support future integration with validated NASA research datasets and compatible medical devices.

The project focuses on improving health-data visibility, supporting early awareness of potential risks, and helping mission control and medical teams review astronaut health information.

Our goal is to develop a scalable software platform that supports astronaut health monitoring without replacing professional medical decisions.
